title: Open substacks and finite etale decorations of a smooth finite-diagonal stack
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack smooth and of finite type over $k$, with finite diagonal. Stack, 2-fibre product and Deligne--Mumford have the meanings in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. An open substack $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal X$ means a full subcategory stable under pullback whose base change by every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ is an open subscheme of $T$. Then $\mathcal U$ is a smooth finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack with finite diagonal. Let $\mathcal Y$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $k$-schemes, with a morphism $p:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal U$. Suppose that for every scheme $T\to\mathcal U$ the 2-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal U}\mathcal Y$ is equivalent, naturally on $T$-schemes, to a scheme finite etale over $T$. Then $\mathcal Y$ is a smooth finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack with finite diagonal, and $p$ is representable finite etale. In particular both $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal Y$ are separated over $k$: separated for a stack means that its diagonal is proper. The empty open and an everywhere empty finite etale decoration are allowed; no surjectivity hypothesis on $p$ is imposed. Finite diagonal means that every scheme base change of the diagonal is finite. Scheme properties use [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]; smoothness and finite type on stacks are tested on smooth atlases, with quasi-compactness for finite type.

source.place: Tags 0CIP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 0CIM (lemma-composition-etale), 075V (lemma-composition-smooth), 06FT (lemma-composition-finite-type), 0CPM (lemma-locally-closed-in-noetherian), 050E (lemma-trivial-implications); algebraicity and effective stack descent: algebraic.tex Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic) and Tag 05UM (lemma-representable-morphism-to-algebraic). Agent-formulated combination including the representable finite-etale chart criterion and finite-diagonal consequence.

proof.text: The full pullback-stable subcategory $\mathcal U$ is fibred in groupoids: pullbacks of its objects stay in it, and fullness supplies exactly the same cartesian lifts as in $\mathcal X$. The stipulated open-scheme pullbacks make $\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ representable by schemes. Apply the representable-fibred-category stack lemma, with base stack $\mathcal X$, to obtain effective etale descent for $\mathcal U$.

For a scheme $T$ and two objects $u_1,u_2$ of $\mathcal U(T)$, fullness gives $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal U}(u_1,u_2)=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X}(u_1,u_2)$ on all $T$-schemes. The latter is a scheme finite over $T$ by the finite-diagonal hypothesis. Thus $\mathcal U$ has representable finite diagonal. Choose the etale surjective atlas $D\to\mathcal X$ from the Deligne--Mumford hypothesis. Its pullback $D_{\mathcal U}=D\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$ is an open subscheme of $D$. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal U$, its pullback is $D\times_{\mathcal X}T$, etale and surjective over $T$ by the defining property of the original atlas. Hence $D_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal U$ is an etale surjective scheme atlas. Together with step 1 this proves that $\mathcal U$ is Deligne--Mumford.

source.place: Definitions of a scheme-representable open subcategory and an atlas; 2-fibre-product objects and arrows

proof.text: Apply the affine smooth atlas lemma to $\mathcal X$, whose Deligne--Mumford atlas is smooth: its scheme base changes are etale, hence smooth by the etale-smoothness lemma, to choose $a:A\to\mathcal X$ with $A$ smooth, affine and finite type over $k$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: it is a single point and its local ring has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$. The finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma therefore makes $A$ Noetherian. Put $A_{\mathcal U}=A\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$, an open subscheme of $A$. The Noetherian-open-subscheme lemma makes $A_{\mathcal U}$ Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); properties.tex Tags 01OW and 01OZ

proof.text: The open-immersion smooth-composition lemma makes $A_{\mathcal U}$ smooth over $k$. It is also finite type over $k$: write $A=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra; quasi-compactness of its open $A_{\mathcal U}$ selects finitely many basic opens $D(f_j)$ covering it. Their coordinate rings $R[1/f_j]$ are generated by the generators of $R$ and $1/f_j$. For any scheme $T\to\mathcal U$, the atlas pullback $A_{\mathcal U}\times_{\mathcal U}T$ identifies with $A\times_{\mathcal X}T$, so it is smooth and surjective. Thus $A_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal U$ is a smooth atlas. The smoothness and local finite type of this chart prove those properties for $\mathcal U$. Its quasi-compactness proves quasi-compactness of $\mathcal U$: pull an open cover back to $A_{\mathcal U}$, choose a finite subcover there, and use surjectivity to see it covers $\mathcal U$. Hence $\mathcal U$ is finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tags 01VC (lemma-open-immersion-smooth), 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth); finite-type definition 01T0; explicit basic-open argument

proof.text: The hypothesis about $T\times_{\mathcal U}\mathcal Y$, including its natural equivalence on all $T$-schemes, says exactly that $p$ is representable by schemes and finite etale after every scheme base change. This proves the asserted representable finite-etale property directly from its definition. Since $\mathcal U$ is now a stack, the representable-fibred-category stack lemma applies to $p$ and makes $\mathcal Y$ a stack. No surjectivity of the represented finite-etale schemes is needed.

source.place: Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic); scheme-test definition of representable finite etale

proof.text: We can now apply the existing representable-finite stack-properties lemma to $p:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal U$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its base is Deligne--Mumford by step 2, its source is a stack by step 5, and its morphism is representable finite by step 5. Its conclusion makes $\mathcal Y$ Deligne--Mumford. Only that conclusion is used here.

source.place: Tag 05UM (lemma-representable-morphism-to-algebraic); Deligne--Mumford consequence of base-changing an etale atlas

proof.text: Fix $y_1,y_2\in\mathcal Y(T)$ for a scheme $T$, and put $u_i=p(y_i)$. By step 2, $I=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal U}(u_1,u_2)$ is a finite $T$-scheme. Over $I$ its universal isomorphism $\alpha:u_1\simeq u_2$ makes $(y_1,\alpha)$ and $(y_2,\mathrm{id})$ sections of the scheme $E=I\times_{u_2,\mathcal U}\mathcal Y$, finite etale over $I$ by hypothesis. Since $E\to I$ is finite, the finite-proper lemma makes it proper and therefore separated; its diagonal is a closed immersion by the definition of properness. The equality locus $J$ of the two sections is consequently a closed subscheme of $I$: it is the inverse image of that diagonal under the pair of sections. Affine-locally the inverse image is cut out by the images of the defining ideal, so is a closed immersion. By the objects-and-arrows definition of the 2-fibre product, over a map to $I$ this equality says exactly that there is an arrow $y_1\simeq y_2$ inducing $\alpha$. Such an arrow, if it exists, is unique because the relative fibre is a discrete represented groupoid. Thus $J$ represents $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(y_1,y_2)$. The closed-immersion-finite and finite-composition lemmas give $J\to I\to T$ finite. This proves finite diagonal for $\mathcal Y$.

source.place: Tags 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite), 01WK (lemma-composition-finite); explicit relative Isom equality-locus construction

proof.text: Set $B=A_{\mathcal U}\times_{\mathcal U}\mathcal Y$. It is a scheme finite etale over $A_{\mathcal U}$. The etale-smoothness lemma makes the etale morphism $B\to A_{\mathcal U}$ smooth. The smooth-composition lemma, applied to $B\to A_{\mathcal U}\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $B$ smooth over $k$. It is finite type over $k$ as well: use the finite basic-open cover $\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f_j]$ of step 4; its inverse images in $B$ are affine by finiteness. Their coordinate algebras $C_j$ are finite modules over $R[1/f_j]$. Choose module generators $c_{j1},\ldots,c_{jn_j}$. The generators of $R[1/f_j]$ as a $k$-algebra, together with these $c_{ji}$, generate $C_j$ as a $k$-algebra, since every element is already a linear combination of the $c_{ji}$. This is a finite affine cover by finitely generated $k$-algebras, exactly finite type.

source.place: Tag 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth); elementary finite-algebra generator argument for finite type

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, the defining 2-fibre products identify $B\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ with $A_{\mathcal U}\times_{\mathcal U}T=A\times_{\mathcal X}T$. These identifications simply forget the intermediate object and its isomorphism, with inverse inserting its pullback; the compatibility equation on arrows is unchanged. Hence $B\to\mathcal Y$ is smooth and surjective by the original atlas test for $A\to\mathcal X$. Smoothness and local finite type of $B$ from step 8 therefore prove smoothness and local finite type of $\mathcal Y$. An open cover of $\mathcal Y$ pulls back to an open cover of the quasi-compact scheme $B$; a finite subcover descends by surjectivity. This proves quasi-compactness, hence finite type of $\mathcal Y$.

source.place: Scheme-test definition of a smooth atlas; explicit 2-fibre-product identity and finite-subcover argument

proof.text: The diagonals of $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal Y$ have finite scheme base changes by steps 2 and 7. Each such finite scheme morphism is proper by the finite-proper lemma. Thus both stack diagonals are proper, which is precisely separatedness in the statement. If $\mathcal U$ is empty, its charts $A_{\mathcal U}$ and $B$ are empty; if the decoration is empty, $B$ and $\mathcal Y$ are empty. All atlas tests, equality loci and finite-cover arguments above allow empty schemes and empty covers, and only the atlas maps, never $p$, have been assumed surjective.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); scheme-test definition of proper diagonal

lean.statement: theorem dm_open_finite_etale_permanence (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hX : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack X) (hft : HasSmoothFiniteTypeModuliAtlas X) (hdiag : HasFiniteModuliDiagonal X) (U : OpenModuliSubstack X) : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack U.category ∧ HasSmoothFiniteTypeModuliAtlas U.category ∧ HasFiniteModuliDiagonal U.category ∧ HasProperModuliDiagonal U.category ∧ ∀ (Y : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (p : BasedFunctor Y U.category), IsFibredInGroupoids Y → (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) U.category), ∃ (E : Over (Spec (.of k))) (g : E ⟶ T) (e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj E)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct t p)), IsFinite g.left ∧ Etale g.left ∧ IsSchemeModuliBaseChange e g) → IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack Y ∧ HasSmoothFiniteTypeModuliAtlas Y ∧ HasFiniteModuliDiagonal Y ∧ IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap p ∧ IsEtaleModuliMap p ∧ HasProperModuliDiagonal Y
